name: umask
description: Sets or shows the permission mask that determines the default permissions of newly created files and directories.

examples.explanation: The typical default: subtract from 666 for files (644) and from 777 for directories (755).
Symbolic form of the same mask.
With mask 077, new files are 600 and directories 700 — nothing readable by group or others (result shown via ls -l).

about: umask removes permission bits from the defaults: files start at 666 (no execute), directories at 777. A mask of 022 removes w for group/others, giving files 644 and directories 755. A mask of 077 removes all group/other bits, giving 600/700. The mask is per-process and inherited from the login shell, PAM, or systemd service settings.
useCases: Make your home directory private: umask 077 in ~/.bashrc.
Tighten defaults for a service by setting UMask= in its systemd unit.
Understand why files created by scripts have "unexpected" permissions.
mistakes: Setting umask in a script and expecting it to affect the parent shell.
Expecting umask to change existing files — it only affects future creations.
